selectionPurpose: Qualitative diagnostic contrasts, deliberately selected rather than representative outcome-rate sample. All 24 selected plays belong to the same strict-clean 302 back-run benchmark cohort.
identityRule: G{gameIndex}-P{native log row.index padded to three digits}; no index+1 transformation.
limits: Light replays preserve positions, facing and event records. Review prompts are questions; do not infer actual assignment, perception, intent or transmitted forces from paths alone. Carrier contact is the engine event, not NFL charted contact. Group contrasts are not controlled causal experiments.

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch both guards: do their first steps establish useful angles, and is the RB choosing a lane opened by those blocks?

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch the RB approach the line and identify the first defender who closes the lane. Do the blocking and approach paths look believable?

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Does the first loss of space come from penetration, a blocker taking a poor path, or the runner meeting traffic? Separate what you see from the cause you suspect.

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch lateral flow, edge leverage and the RB turn upfield. Are the pursuit angles and braking plausible?

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Where does the outside path close, and does the RB have a visible alternative? Watch whether the blocker can physically reach his opponent.

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Compare with the other Outside Zone clips: does the handoff-to-cut timing look natural before the defender arrives?

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Follow the pulling lineman, then the RB. Do the path, arrival angle and collision create a plausible lane?

plays.groupLabel: Ordinary runs: establish a baseline
plays.reviewPrompt: Does the puller get a workable angle before contact, and does the RB arrive before or after the lane closes?

plays.groupLabel: Interior timing: Counter, Trap and Draw
plays.reviewPrompt: Follow both pulling blockers before watching the ball. Which path first becomes obstructed, and how does each blocker respond?

plays.groupLabel: Interior timing: Counter, Trap and Draw
plays.reviewPrompt: Find the earliest breakdown before the tackle: is the visible problem the pulling path, backfield congestion, penetration or the runner timing?

plays.groupLabel: Interior timing: Counter, Trap and Draw
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch puller clearance and contact angles in the condensed front. Does anyone visibly abandon useful work or get stuck between jobs?

plays.groupLabel: Interior timing: Counter, Trap and Draw
plays.reviewPrompt: A less unsuccessful Counter, not a benchmark success. Compare puller timing and usable space with the failures.

plays.groupLabel: Interior timing: Counter, Trap and Draw
plays.reviewPrompt: The one clean Counter reaching the benchmark success threshold in this sample. What develops differently before the explosive part begins?

plays.groupLabel: Interior timing: Counter, Trap and Draw
plays.reviewPrompt: Follow the trapping guard toward the interior defender. Is his contact angle attainable, and does the RB arrive with any usable lane?

plays.groupLabel: Interior timing: Counter, Trap and Draw
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch the early pass-like presentation and the interior opening. Is the runner reading an opening that never exists, or does it close before arrival?

plays.groupLabel: Short yardage and the goal line
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch the initial push and RB decision. Does the gain come through a realistic small crease rather than a sudden speed or balance jump?

plays.groupLabel: Short yardage and the goal line
plays.reviewPrompt: Compare initial contact and finish with the third-and-one clip. Does the spot and final movement look consistent with the collision?

plays.groupLabel: Short yardage and the goal line
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch the initial double-team geometry, runner finish and bodies near the goal line. Does the short gain look mechanically earned?

plays.groupLabel: Short yardage and the goal line
plays.reviewLabel: Wide Zone close to the goal line
plays.reviewPrompt: With only 6.9 yards to the end zone, watch edge space, turn-up decision and defensive pursuit. Do the boundaries affect movement plausibly?

plays.groupLabel: Breakaway audit: where does a run become a touchdown?
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch the first three seconds, then the first carrier contact and the last defender with a realistic angle. Where does the ordinary gain become a breakaway?

plays.groupLabel: Breakaway audit: where does a run become a touchdown?
plays.reviewPrompt: Watch which defender can first close the edge and each recorded missed tackle after the cut. Do the misses look achievable rather than everyone over-running? This play has no recorded carrier-contact event.

plays.groupLabel: Breakaway audit: where does a run become a touchdown?
plays.reviewPrompt: Follow the nearest safety from before the handoff through his first approach. Does his acceleration, braking and angle look believable?
